avis.texte: I'm surpised that this product has good reviews. Like others have mentioned, it does NOT remove makeup- ESPECIALLY NOT WATERPROOF MAKEUP! I tried it with all of my usual waterproof makeup, and I had to SCRUB really hard 3-4 times with re-applying the product, using WAY more than a pea-sized amount. I know I have sensitive skin and eyes, and I've been searching for one that doesn't make my eyes burn, this one made my eyes burn and I'll be continuing my search for a better makeup remover.

I love all the Byoma products I've used so far, but this one is just bad- I'm shocked it has any positive reviews. I've been using it for a few months now, hoping it would grow on me, but no. It's very oily and repels water even after it's emulsified and turned milky. Just feels like you rubbed vaseline on your face. And it doesnt remove makup AT ALL. I dont even where waterproof products. Plain water removes my makeup better than this stuff. It barely makes makeup budge - it takes 2-3 times for me to get any of it off and it ends up just making makeup smear and stick to my face. And your face feels so gross after using it, so you have to use another cleanser to get the gross vaseline feeling off. The only MAYBE good thing i can say is that it doesnt dehydrate my face like other cleasners - if you can even truly call this a cleanser. Don't waste hour money, y'all.

I have been using this product for a while now and I really like it. The price for what you get is a little high but it has done really well with my skin. It's definitely oil based so probably not the best for oily skin. This cleanser left my skin feeling really hydrated and my skin didn't feel stripped. I do have to say it does have a weird smell. When I first used it I thought it smelled like clay but I quickly got over it once I saw what it was doing for my skin. This cleanser is also really great at removing makeup, although I want to mention that to take off mascara you have to wash your face twice. I don't believe that this melting balm was meant to be a makeup remover but it does a pretty great job. When you first put the product in your hands it feels almost like a putty, but the second you rub it into your face it becomes an oil. After you rub it into your face it does take a bit of effort to wash it off. When water gets mixed with the melting balm it becomes a really milky white and from there it is easy to remove.
This does not work to remove mascara or eyeliner. Even if I dip in multiple times and use a wash cloth it does not remove my mascara basically at all. You are better off with ELF

As far as cleansing balms go, this one did a fine job - removed all traces of makeup and mascara easily, rinsed cleanly, and has no perceptible odour. I will not buy it again, however, due to how overpackaged it is. You think the container will be full of product, but inside, there is a smaller round compartment holding the balm (another user posted an image of this). It is - quite frankly - outrageous. While several other brands are making an effort to reduce plastic packaging, BYOMA seems to want to use MORE plastic. In fact, I have purchased several BYOMA products and find they all suffer from this (though the balm is the worst offender). The products are fine, but they're not "holy grail" type products, and definitely not worth all the plastic waste that they produce

product worked decent for taking face makeup off once the weird top layer of product came off. Kind of expensive for the amount you are getting, but its one of the balm cleansers that doesnt make ur eyes blurry.

I always follow-up with my cleanser and I can say I've noticed serious improvement with my skin. I will definitely be repurchasing.

avis.titre: Did I get the same product??
avis.texte: I have read all the reviews and I'm actually shocked! I have almost finished this container of cleansing balm and the only thing that I can really complain about is mascara is a little more difficult to remove than I would like. Having said that, it still does a fine job. I don't notice any weird medicinal scent to it. It melts into the skin very fast and it rinses off just fine. This is meant to be a first cleanse anyway, so if there is actually any residue left over, your other cleanser is going to remove it, but I don't have an issue with any kind of residue. This balm is thick and creamy in an emollient type of way but instantly turns into an oil like texture when you start rubbing it in. It melts makeup on contact and as far as the mascara issue I have, I just let the balm sit on my lashes while I'm rubbing it in on the rest of my face and it comes off fine. I guess in the end it's all about preference, but I like cleansing balms that are softer in texture like this one and not the ones you have to have a spoon to scoop out the harder balms that never seem to melt completely. This one also emulsifies really well when you add warm water to it. Overall, it is a very good cleansing balm and it feels really nice on the skin and doesn't leave your skin feeling stripped afterwards. There is a size discrepancy listed by Ulta as 3.38oz vs the picture of the product showing a size of 2.12oz so be aware of that.

ive tried LOTS of makeuo removing balms and this is my fav. affordable and completey removes all of my makeups! tbh elemis burned my eyes, felt like tea tree oil in my eyes. no burning with this! will abs repurchase!

Somehow over looked the rosemary essential oil when I was reading the ingredients. I think this product would be so much better without it because the rest of the ingredients are fine. It made my skin really dry and super irritated, it would sting to put my products on after (and my products are amazing, all acne-safe and super hydrating, all recommended by my esthetician and I have been using them for years but wanted to look for a cheaper pre-cleanse). Now I have some tiny pimples around my cheeks and chin, and I'm peeling. Luckily the rest of my routine is solid so that helped keep this under control cause I think it could have been a lot worse otherwise.

I have been on the hunt for a cruelty-free, polyethylene-free cleansing balm since Ulta stopped selling my last two favorites. This one fit the bill, so I gave it a shot. The actual product is really nice! It is super smooth, melts easily, removes makeup and sunscreen, emulsifies well, and rinses away easily. Overall I really, really like it. One thing I'm pretty neutral about is scent, especially in a rinse off product. People who are incredibly sensitive to scent might have an issue with this. It doesn't have like a super strong added artificial fragrance, but rather a very, very slight medicinal scent. It kind of smells like Vicks Vaporub, but it isn't unpleasant and not strong at all. Plus it rinses away immediately. My biggest gripe is the packaging. Sure, it looks nice. The colors and design are pleasing, I like the cube shape. However, for a "sustainable packaging brand" the ratio of plastic packaging to actual product is wild. The packaging is big and bulky and takes up a lot of precious counter space, plus it kind of makes you think you are getting far more product than you actually are. Overall, it's a great product that works well. It does have a very slight scent, and in my opinion the packaging is just too bulky.

For this balm, you have to massage it really well into the skin with wet hands in order for it to melt away the makeup. I do find that for eye makeup, I have to use a wet paper towel to help take off the residual mascara it leaves underneath my eyes. I really like the smell, smells floral/herbally, really clean scent.

This is a great cleanser that breaks down makeup and great for an at home facial. A little goes a long way. Idk why so many people complain about the smell, it is not a pungent smell, it smells natural. Idk why everyone wants fragrance in everything. This product works really well a d leaves rhe face feeling smooth abd moisturized after using.

This balm is amazing. I wear pretty heavy makeup, and I'd say, a dab of this, about the size of a quarter gets ALL my makeup off. I use it dry and you just have to wet your fingers and rub them over your face to emulsify it and then you rinse and BAM. ALL GONE. I dont even need a second cleanser like I have with oil washes in the past. I have oily skin as well and it doesn't make me feel oily.

avis.titre: Not bad, but not great either
avis.texte: This does remove makeup, sunscreen, etc. but on heavier makeup days or waterproof makeup days, i do find that I need to use a washcloth or cotton pad to assist. The texture is really nice. Its on the thicker side of the cleansing balm spectrum but its smooth and creamy. It emuslifies and rinses clean. The biggest downfall is that it does sting my eyes pretty bad and also makes my vision blurry even after a double cleanse. Its good enough to finish the jar, but I won't be repurchasing.

I was pleasantly suprised with this cleansing balm. For the price its an excellent choice. Goes on smoothly. Removes makeup well. Only issues sometimes it doesnt get all of my waterproof mascara off. But usually my 2nd cleanse gets whatever is left over. Im also not a fan of the smell, but its a light scent and is only on my face for a min. Overall excellent product, works as well if not better than some of the more expensive balms.

So I've been on the hunt for a cleansing balm that is microplastics free, and this is one that came up so I decided to try it. Um, it's really really thick. Not in a good way like the "oh this'll melt into the skin really nice and remove everything" way, but in a bad way like "oh crap I forgot my squeezy tube lip balm in my car in the middle of winter and now I need to put it in my bra for five minutes to warm it up" way. And even then it STILL doesn't melt enough. You'd think that with it being so thick, it would at least melt everything away, right? Wrong! It doesn't remove makeup that well, and I don't wear a ton of makeup. I've used it on heavy makeup days, light makeup days, and days where all Ive put on is sunscreen, and it's never really felt totally clean, and I would have to double cleanse with my regular cleanser, which because I have very dry and sensitizing skin I don't use a gel cleanser, I use a cream cleanser. It also takes a long time to wash off completely, and even when it's washed off completely the smell of it lingers. A lot of people have said it smells like Vicks and it kind of does, but I feel it smells more like Amrut Malam which is an Indian ointment which is used for everything by Indians in the same way Latines use Vicks (I'm Indian and Latine, so these have been staples in my house and while they do smell similar, it's still a very different scent.) Anyways, whether it smells more like one or the other isn't that important, it just smells medicinal
The smell wasnt that pleasant, but the product removes makeup easily. I would recommend.
